match.reason: The closest bank point covers scams in general and identity theft, while this point is specifically about investment scams, with high-return promises, unlicensed advisers and checking ASIC Moneysmart, so it teaches a different and narrower idea.

draft.title: Investment scams
card: An investment scam is a trick that takes your money by offering a fake or dishonest investment. Scammers target people of any age, including young people.
A warning sign is a promise of high returns with no risk. Real investments that can earn more usually carry more risk, so a promise of big profits with no chance of loss is not believable.
Other warning signs are pressure to act fast, such as "only 24 hours left", and an adviser who is not licensed. A genuine business gives you time to think and check.

Before investing, check the business on ASIC's Moneysmart website, which lists licensed businesses. ASIC is the Australian Securities and Investments Commission. If it is not on the list, do not hand over money.
draft.remember: Big returns with no risk, pressure to hurry and no licence are all signs of a scam. Check Moneysmart first.

a.q: Which offer shows the clearest sign of an investment scam?
opts: A promise of 30% a year with no risk of loss
A fund that says its returns can go up or down
An adviser who lists their licence details
A bank account that pays a low rate of interest
a.why: Higher returns usually come with higher risk, so a high return with no risk cannot be trusted. The fund that says returns can fall is being honest about risk, which is what real investments do.
a.clue: Which offer ignores the link between risk and return?

b.q: Jay gets a call from a man offering shares in a mining company. He says the offer ends tonight. What should Jay do first?
opts: Check if the business is licensed on Moneysmart
Pay a small deposit to hold the offer until tomorrow
Ask the caller whether he is a licensed adviser
Invest only if friends say the company seems good
b.why: Moneysmart lists licensed businesses, so it is an independent check. Asking the caller proves nothing, because a scammer can simply say yes. The deadline is itself pressure to act fast, so paying a deposit would be giving in to it.
b.clue: Trust a source that does not depend on what the caller says.

a.best: A promise of 30% a year with no risk of loss

b.best: Check if the business is licensed on Moneysmart
